seoTitle: How to Fix ChatGPT 'Conversation Not Found' Error
metaDescription: Resolve the ChatGPT 'Conversation Not Found' error caused by expired sessions, deleted chats, or stale browser cache, with the exact settings to check.
intro: Opening an old ChatGPT thread only to see "Conversation not found" is jarring, especially when you were counting on that chat history being there. The error usually comes down to one of a few causes: an expired session, a chat that was actually deleted, or cached browser data getting in the way of a fresh load. This guide walks through the fixes in order of how likely they are to work, starting with the quickest and ending with checking whether the problem is on OpenAI's end rather than yours.

steps.heading: Recognize what the error actually looks like
steps.body: The error shows up as a red-bordered banner reading "Conversation not found" directly inside the chat thread, usually paired with "There was an error generating a response" and a Regenerate button underneath. Seeing this doesn't necessarily mean your chat history is gone for good — in most cases it's a loading or session problem rather than permanent data loss, which is why the fixes below start simple.

image.caption: The "Conversation not found" error as it appears inside a ChatGPT thread, with a Regenerate option below it.

steps.heading: Refresh the page and log back in
steps.body: Start with the obvious fix: reload the page or fully close and reopen the app. If that doesn't clear it, sign out of ChatGPT completely and log back in — this forces a new session token and resolves the error when it's caused by an expired or corrupted session rather than a genuinely missing conversation. Logging out doesn't delete any of your other saved chats, so there's no downside to trying it first.

steps.heading: Open your browser's site settings
steps.body: If refreshing and re-logging in doesn't help, the next step is clearing stale data your browser has cached for ChatGPT. From Chrome's menu, go into Settings, then Privacy and security, then All sites to see every site storing data in your browser along with how much space each one uses. This is also a useful moment to notice how much unrelated data has piled up across other sites — it's normal for this list to be long.

image.caption: Chrome's All sites view under Privacy and security, listing every site with stored data and how much each one is using.

steps.heading: Clear cached data for chatgpt.com specifically
steps.body: Instead of wiping everything, search the All sites list for "chatgpt" to isolate just chatgpt.com's stored data — cookies and site storage. Click the trash icon next to it and confirm the deletion. This clears out corrupted cache or cookies without touching your saved passwords, autofill, or history for every other site you use, which is a much safer move than a blanket "clear all browsing data."

image.caption: Searching Chrome's All sites list down to just chatgpt.com, ready to delete its stored cookies and data.

steps.heading: Reload ChatGPT and check the conversation again
steps.body: After clearing chatgpt.com's data, reload the site and log back in. Navigate to the conversation that previously showed the error. If it loads normally now, the issue was stale cache. If the same "Conversation not found" message appears again immediately, that's a stronger sign the chat itself was deleted rather than a caching glitch — deleted conversations can't be recovered through any of these steps.

steps.heading: Check OpenAI's status page for server issues
steps.body: If the error is happening across multiple conversations or devices, or your account otherwise seems fine, check OpenAI's status page for reported incidents. A widespread "conversation not found" wave that clears up on its own after a short wait is usually a server-side hiccup rather than anything specific to your account, and there's nothing to fix locally in that case beyond waiting it out.

steps.heading: Update the ChatGPT app on mobile
steps.body: On mobile, an outdated app version can trigger the same error even when the web version works fine. Check your device's app store for a pending ChatGPT update, install it, and restart the app before trying the conversation again. Keeping the app current also avoids a handful of other sync issues between mobile and desktop chat history.

faq.question: Can a deleted ChatGPT conversation be recovered?
faq.answer: No, once a conversation is deleted it generally can't be restored, which is one of the more common permanent causes behind this error.

faq.question: Is this error the same on the mobile app and website?
faq.answer: The underlying causes are similar, but the fix differs slightly — on the web you clear the site's cached data in your browser settings, while on mobile the more common fix is updating the app itself.

faq.question: Will logging out delete my other saved chats?
faq.answer: No, logging out and back in only refreshes your session token — it doesn't delete or affect any of your other saved conversations.

faq.question: How do I know if it's a server-wide issue?
faq.answer: Check OpenAI's status page for reported incidents. If the error is showing up broadly for other users too, it's likely temporary and on OpenAI's end rather than something to fix on your device.

faq.question: Do I need to clear my entire browser cache?
faq.answer: No. Searching Chrome's All sites list for chatgpt.com and deleting just that site's stored data is enough, and it avoids wiping cookies, logins, or saved data for every other site you use.
